raw.assessment: The incumbent produces the required embedded-caption format and retains earlier previews. It reached the timing target in 20/30 sessions, below the required 27/30. Unexpected caption versions in four downloads, including one earlier video cut, establish version uncertainty but do not establish its cause. Completion-order numbering, out-of-order renders and incomplete pairing records plausibly contribute. H1-O7 limits any claim that full rendering itself is generally unsuitable: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in five to 11 minutes without reported uncertainty. Waiting, selection and review time remain unseparated. The sampled 49 processing hours do not establish festival capacity. All observations are stipulated synthetic evidence.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: bind each request to immutable caption and video snapshots, identify its preview by that pair, and verify the rendered inputs against that binding before exposing it for delivery. Retain the delivered pair and original caption text while replacements are prepared.
openings.delta: Make intended input identity explicit and independent of completion sequence or editor filenames.
openings.prediction: With completion order deliberately reversed, editors still select the intended pair and a mismatched input pair is rejected before delivery.
openings.probe: On private staging with demonstration footage, request two caption revisions and two video cuts, reverse completion order, and introduce a mismatched input. Have the two editors identify the intended preview and retrieve the previous delivery's original wording; compare selected and rendered input hashes with the request binding.
assumptions: Existing storage can retain immutable inputs without exceeding the allowance.
Binding, verification and interface changes fit four engineer-days and testing fits one editor-day.
The worker can report its actual consumed inputs.

openings.claim: In slow sessions, does the correct preview become available late, or does identification and review consume the remaining time after it is available?
openings.delta: Discriminate production delay from post-availability delay before choosing another intervention.
openings.prediction: A production-delay account predicts late availability of the correct pair; an identification/review account predicts earlier availability followed by a long interval to verified selection. Both may contribute.
openings.probe: Join timestamped render events to intended input pairs and collect a brief private editor trace marking final edit, correct preview availability, selection and completed review. Compare these intervals for single-correction and repeated-edit sessions; separately record queue and render duration where timestamps permit.
assumptions: A bounded trace study fits the existing editor-day and engineering budget.
Correct-pair availability can be reconstructed; otherwise the study must be prospective.

raw.assessment: The observed 20/30 timely sessions fall below the target. Reversed completion order and unexpected source versions justify investigating identity and scheduling, but do not establish whether delays arise from rendering or editor interpretation. The nine uncomplicated correction sessions show that acceptable performance already occurs in some conditions.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: bind each preview request to immutable video and caption snapshots, and display that pair beside its result. Keep the delivered pair pinned with its original text; completion order must not redefine the editor's selected target.
openings.delta: Replace filename/sequential-number inference with a persistent request identity shared by input selection, worker reads and preview history.
openings.prediction: Reversed completion will leave the selected target identifiable. Delivered previews will match the explicitly intended source pair, provided that pair was selected correctly.
openings.probe: In private staging, alternate two demonstration cuts and caption revisions, deliberately reverse completion, and compare requested hashes, worker inputs and visible output. Ask editors to identify the intended preview and retrieve the pinned delivered wording. Reject any unintended pairing.
assumptions: Snapshot references remain immutable and accessible on existing accounts.
Implementation and verification fit two engineer-days and half an editor-day.
Existing embedded-caption delivery rendering is retained.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: save caption drafts immediately but start full rendering through an explicit Preview action that captures the chosen source pair. Show when the saved draft differs from the requested preview.
openings.delta: Separate draft persistence from expensive preview generation so intermediate saves need not each consume a render.
openings.prediction: Render requests per session decrease if editors consolidate saves. Timeliness improves only where avoided renders reduce relevant waiting; an extra action could instead delay preview requests.
openings.probe: Instrument final-edit-to-request, queue, render and selection/watch intervals. Across 30 new sessions, require at least 27 correctly identified previews within 15 minutes and zero unintended delivered pairings. Record render count and processing hours; retain delivered history and stop processing before the weekly allowance is exceeded.
assumptions: Implementation and editor evaluation fit the remaining two engineer-days and half editor-day.
Staging and operational processing together stay within 80 hours weekly.
Editors recognize draft/preview differences; festival capacity remains unestablished.

openings.claim: Bind immutable caption/video pairs across request, worker and displayed result; verify consumed inputs before delivery. Preserve selected target despite completion order; pin delivered pair and original text.
openings.discriminator: Reversed completion preserves identification; mismatched inputs block delivery.
openings.fit: Private accounts, embedded format and delivered-history access preserved; budget fit uncertain.
openings.probe: Alternate two demonstration cuts/revisions, reverse completion, inject mismatch; compare requested/consumed/output hashes and editor identification plus prior-wording retrieval.
openings.uncertainty: Correct intended-pair selection, immutable storage capacity and worker reporting assumed; A1's two engineer-days/half editor-day estimate unverified.

openings.claim: Separate correct-preview production delay from subsequent identification/review delay; both may contribute.
openings.discriminator: Correct-pair availability late versus early with delayed selection/review.
openings.fit: Bounded private trace; study budget uncertain.
openings.probe: Join events to intended pairs; trace final edit, availability, selection and completed review; separate queue/render; compare single-correction and repeated-edit sessions.
openings.uncertainty: Pair reconstruction may require prospective tracing. Nine successful correction sessions limit general rendering criticism.

openings.claim: Save drafts immediately; explicit Preview captures selected pair and displays draft/request differences, reducing intermediate renders.
openings.discriminator: Fewer requests improve timing only through reduced relevant waiting; extra action may delay requests.
openings.fit: Retain private processing, embedded delivery and delivered history; enforce 80 hours including staging.
openings.probe: Measure edit-to-request, queue, render, selection/watch, render count and hours; 30 sessions require 27 timely correct previews and zero unintended deliveries.
openings.uncertainty: Editors must consolidate saves and recognize differences; remaining two engineer-days/half editor-day and festival capacity unverified.

lineage.reason: With Z1; preserve visible identity and stable selection.

post_distill.decision: Probe identity and timing first; condition Preview-action adoption on waiting evidence. Synthetic observations establish neither cause nor improvement; combined work must fit four engineer-days/one editor-day.
